entities.summary: Vigrahapala II, the tenth ruler of the Pala line, succeeded his predecessor Gopala III in the Bengal region of the Indian subcontinent in 976 CE. He reigned for at least 12 years, during which time he implemented various administrative reforms and expanded the empire's borders. Vigrahapala II's reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against neighboring kingdoms, which ultimately led to the empire's decline. Despite this, he is remembered for his efforts to promote Buddhism and his patronage of scholars and artists. The legacy of Vigrahapala II can be seen in the continued influence of Pala art and architecture in the region, as well as the preservation of ancient texts and manuscripts. The impact of his reign can also be felt in the modern-day cultural and economic landscape of Bengal, which continues to be shaped by the region's rich history and cultural heritage.
